articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Traded to Cowboys in New NFL Rumors Following Steelers Contract Standoff
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly moving on from starting cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after stalled extension negotiations.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly moving on from starting cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after stalled extension negotiations.

The Steelers traded Porter to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday, per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer. ESPN's Todd Archer provided details on the deal:

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

Despite the trade, the Cowboys don't plan to sign Porter to an extension immediately and will instead play out the year on his current deal, per NFL Insider Jordan Schultz .

Porter, who has not yet played this season, is under a $4.9 million cap hit in the final year of his rookie contract .

The Steelers attempted to finalize an extension for Porter this offseason but did not come to resolution before the franchise's Week 1 negotiating deadline, which general manager Omar Khan told reporters in August the franchise did not plan to change.

Porter was placed on the PUP list in early August after reportedly aggravating a back injury. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said later that month the team was at an "impasse" in contract negotiations with Porter.

The cornerback ultimately missed the first three games for the Steelers before he was traded without having played a snap in 2026.

The news comes after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the Cowboys had joined teams including the Detroit Lions in making inquiries about Porter.

The Cowboys ultimately won that potential bidding war as part of the team's ongoing effort to overhaul its defense.

Dallas started last season by acquiring Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams, then added Rashan Gary before drafting Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence last spring.

The Cowboys will now continue that effort by addressing the secondary, which struggled early this season after losing Cobie Durant to injury.

Dallas will hope adding more pass protection will help the team improve on a 1-2 start to the season.

Porter missed three games due to injuries last season, including two with a hamstring issue and one with a hip injury.

When available he recorded 52 tackles, 14 passes defensed, a sack and an interception while playing 94 percent of the Steelers' defensive snaps.

Those snaps were mostly run defense and coverage, per Pro Football Focus . Porter ranked top-five in the NFL in yards allowed per coverage snap last season, per PFSN .

Porter has not allowed a touchdown on a regular-season coverage snap since Week 8 of the 2023 season, per NFL Next Gen Stats cited by former NFL scout Matt Williamson .

His defensive efforts down the stretch were a key reason the Steelers made it into the playoffs before losing in the Wild Card round to the Houston Texans.

The Steelers responded to that playoff loss by bringing in McCarthy to replace longtime head coach Mike Tomlin this offseason.

McCarthy, who said in August he would like to coach Porter, will now hope to see his franchise make some more moves ahead of the deadline in order to bolster their secondary in Porter's absence.

articles.title: Steelers trading CB Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys after failed contract negotiations
articles.summary: Porter is in the final year of his rookie deal.
articles.body:
The Steelers are receiving a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round selection from the Cowboys , Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein confirmed .

After being selected with a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Porter is playing in the final year of his rookie deal, which will pay him $3.924 million. Porter and the Steelers were unable to reach a contract extension in the offseason.

Porter won't get an imminent extension in Dallas, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Porter hasn't asked for one yet either, the Dallas Morning News' Calvin Watkins reported .

Pittsburgh general manager Omar Khan had reiterated on Aug. 31 that the team does not deal with extensions during the season, and no deal was completed when the Steelers took on the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1.

Porter has not played this season and was ruled out of the Steelers' Thursday night game against the Browns. He has been listed with a back injury, but many believed his contract situation played a role in his missing the game. It's yet to be seen if he'll play for the Cowboys on Sunday.

Reports earlier in the day indicated that the Lions and Giants offered third-round picks for Porter , but no team had floated a second-rounder. Apparently that changed on Wednesday night.

Porter is the third Steelers player traded to the Cowboys in a 17-month span. In May 2025, the Cowboys acquired wide receiver George Pickens and a 2027 sixth-round pick for a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth. In August, the Cowboys sent a pair of 2027 draft picks (third and sixth) to Pittsburgh in exchange for tackle Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder.

The cornerback likely wanted to be paid like a top player at his position, but after Christian Gonzalez (four-year, $135 million) and Devon Witherspoon (four-year, $132 million) signed mega deals this offseason, Pittsburgh opted not to pursue a record-setting deal and made a trade.

Porter was drafted with the 32nd overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, which was technically the first pick of the second round. The Miami Dolphins had their pick forfeited after the league found them guilty of tampering.

As a rookie, Porter played in all 17 games, starting 11. The corner had 43 total tackles, 1 interception and 10 passes defended.

Over his three-year career, Porter has tallied 165 combined tackles, 3 interceptions and 31 passes defended. Last year, the corner played in 14 games and finished with 52 total tackles, one sack, one interception and 14 passes defended.

The cornerback is the son of former NFL player and Steelers star Joey Porter. He was a linebacker in the NFL from 1999 to 2011, splitting time between the Steelers, Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals . Over the course of his career, he tallied 689 total tackles with 12 interceptions in 188 games.

articles.title: Grade the trade: Cowboys get CB Joey Porter Jr. from Steelers
articles.summary: The Cowboys added an impact defensive player to help on that side of the ball.
articles.body:
Jerry Jones said before the season that he was itching to make another big trade .

The Dallas Cowboys owner made a move, with room to possibly make another splash before November's trade deadline. Dallas dealt a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for their young cornerback Joey Porter Jr., a second-round selection in 2023, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein . Netflix's Tom Pelissero initially reported the trade .

It wasn't the all-in move that Jones has teased. But it's still a big move that should help improve a defense that hasn't been great to start the 2026 season .

Here are the grades for the late Wednesday night trade:

Porter had started to become a distraction for the Steelers. He was seeking a contract extension, it didn't get done, and then he was sitting out games. A back injury was the official reason he hasn't played yet this regular season, but it was hard to believe that his absences weren't contract related.

The move continues to add to a Dallas defense that was horrible last season. The Cowboys made several offseason additions, including at coordinator with the hire of Christian Parker, though there hasn't been a big turnaround. The Cowboys have given up the third-most yards in the NFL this season. Their secondary has given up seven touchdowns with no interceptions. Of 99 qualified corners for Pro Football Focus' grades this season, no Cowboys cornerback ranks in the top 50. DaRon Bland is 55th, Cobie Durant is 67th and Shavon Revel is 85th. Durant is dealing with a hamstring injury that will likely keep him out of this week's game against the Houston Texans , and Revel didn't practice Wednesday with knee and ankle injuries.

Porter helps right away, assuming he can play soon. It will be costly over time. The second-round pick the Cowboys gave up is valuable, and Porter is going to want a big contract extension. He has a lot of leverage after the Cowboys gave up picks to get him. It's a fine move that helps a defense that needed a boost in a wide-open NFC East. But it wasn't cheap.

Pittsburgh wasn't as high on Porter as he was on himself because a contract extension never happened. ESPN's Dan Graziano suggested Porter wanted to be paid $30 million per season. Only six cornerbacks are making that per season.

Pittsburgh had an issue on its hands because Porter wasn't playing, and it seems like more than a coincidence that he hasn't played yet this season while he's also upset about his contract.

"My back has its moments where [there's] a flare up here and there, and we're still just trying to get my conditioning down to just me being out there as much as possible," Porter said this week .

Porter was a hit for the Steelers in the second round three years ago. He became a very good player, though perhaps not one worth the top of the pay scale at cornerback. His PFF grade last season ranked him 36th among cornerbacks — the best grade of his first three NFL seasons — and he has not been named to a Pro Bowl.

The Steelers used a second-rounder to get Porter and after three seasons they got a second-round pick back for him, while adding that sixth-rounder. They won't pay Porter a costly extension.

It's not fun to let go of a good homegrown starter, but it was also going to be hard for the Steelers to find a trade partner that would give up a second-round pick knowing Porter also is seeking a big extension. The Steelers pulled that off, and their Porter drama is over. It's not an ideal ending but it solves some issues.

articles.title: As Jerry Jones' 84th birthday nears, Cowboys' trade for Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is a fitting early birthday present
articles.summary: Dallas sits at 1-2 with a need to improve in several areas. But its offense is explosive, and the cost to acquire Porter shouldn't hurt their immediate windo...
articles.body:
Sometimes, Jerry Jones sticks to talking a big game.

Other times, the Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager puts his money — and draft capital — where his mouth is.

After Jones told reporters on Sept. 20 that "there's nothing more dangerous than an old man with money," the Cowboys have upgraded their secondary.

Schematically, first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker's case for hiring came in part on the basis of how he elevated the Philadelphia Eagles secondary in 2024 and 2025. His talent collection there included 2024 first-round cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and 2024 second-round safety Cooper DeJean .

The Cowboys showed a commitment to upgrading their secondary when they traded up to select safety Caleb Downs 11th overall in the spring. There was still need for more talent if Dallas' defense was going to survive while its high-powered offense thrived. Changing the Cowboys to a 3-4 base defense for the first time in 13 years was going to require some personnel adjustments.

Jones' looming 84th birthday, and the expiration of star receiver George Pickens ' contract this spring, were each reasons to lean into a 2026 contention window.

"We're right on top of it," Jerry Jones told Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday when asked about Porter. "We're very aware of the moving parts out here. We should be. And communication is a big part of it … communication at all levels. At my level, at Stephen's level, at the scouts' level. We all have contacts and this is a time where you really can have discussions and they could be productive.

"Yes, there are conversations going on."

Since the Steelers selected Porter in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, he's started 41 games, deflected 31 passes and intercepted three balls. Porter combined for 165 tackles and three tackles for loss in Pittsburgh.

He didn't play the first three weeks of this season after negotiations reached a point of contention, instead sidelined with what the injury report described as a back issue.

The Steelers ruled Porter out for Thursday night's game against the Cleveland Browns . He increasingly seemed available. And the Cowboys, whose Rio de Janeiro implosion against the Baltimore Ravens included a 27-yard completion in the final seven seconds of the game, increasingly needed help. Their starting core was light. Injuries had left their secondary still thinner.

And the NFC East appears wide open. The New York Giants , since beating the Cowboys in Week 1, have lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart and top pass rusher Brian Burns to season-ending injuries. The Philadelphia Eagles lost to a third-string quarterback on Monday night in Chicago . The Washington Commanders are 1-2 and dealing with an injury to QB Jayden Daniels .

Dallas sits at 1-2 with a need to improve in several areas. But its offense is explosive, and the cost to acquire Porter shouldn't hurt their immediate window. So a Cowboys team that spent several years quiet on the in-season trade market continued its trend of activity that began last year with a deadline acquisition of defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . A Cowboys team that's become familiar with Steelers decision-makers from recent trades for Pickens and left tackle Broderick Jones hit speed dial to run it back one more time.

On Oct. 13, Jones will turn 84. Wednesday night, as September became October for the Steelers and Cowboys, Jones gifted himself an early birthday present.

articles.title: ‘Steelers Keep Getting Fleeced by Dallas,’ ‘THAT’S CRAZY’ — NFL World Reacts to Cowboys Landing Joey Porter Jr. in Blockbuster Trade
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have witnessed a difficult start to the season despite entering the year with plenty of offseason hype, dropping to 1-2 following their We...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have witnessed a difficult start to the season despite entering the year with plenty of offseason hype, dropping to 1-2 following their Week 3 loss. With head coach Brian Schottenheimer preparing the Cowboys for their Week 4 matchup against the Houston Texans , the team has also made headlines by reportedly acquiring Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

NFL World Erupts After Steelers Trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys

Just three days before Wednesday's trade, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that several teams, including the Cowboys and Detroit Lions , had started exploring the possibility of acquiring Porter. He had been seeking a contract extension, but Pittsburgh has traditionally avoided negotiating new deals during the season.

Porter said last week that he would "definitely" play at some point this season, while also saying he had not requested a trade. The subsequent trade, however, changed that outcome.

According to Ari Meirov, Pittsburgh would receive a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for Porter.

Porter has yet to appear in a game this season as he continues to work his way back from a lingering back injury. He had been listed as a full participant in practice but was ruled out of Pittsburgh's Thursday night matchup with Cleveland because of his back issue before the trade was finalized.

Meanwhile, Porter's trade immediately drew reactions from across the NFL world.

"Joey Porter Jr's back injury just cleared right up!" Fantasy Points' injury analyst Jeff Muller wrote .

"Playoff Baseball rocks. But Joey Porter Jr. just got traded to the Cowboys… THAT'S CRAZY," ESPN's Sam Block wrote .

Dallas has been aggressive in reshaping its defense, acquiring Quinnen Williams , Rashan Gary , and Kenny Clark via trades while also using first-round picks on Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence.

Meanwhile, Porter gives Dallas another option at cornerback, an area where the Cowboys have dealt with inconsistency early in the 2026 season. If he can return to full health, his arrival could strengthen a Dallas secondary that has struggled for consistency early in the season.

From Pittsburgh's perspective, the emergence of Asante Samuel Jr . and Daylen Everette gives the Steelers additional options at cornerback following Porter's departure.

Meanwhile, some were clearly dissatisfied with the move.

"Steelers haven't learned. They keep getting fleeced by Dallas huh," one said .

Steelers Depot's Alex Kozora also questioned the move, writing : "The third trade between the Steelers and Cowboys the last two years. George Pickens , Broderick Jones , and now Joey Porter Jr. Crazy how we got here but felt like this was Pittsburgh's only move left. #Steelers."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"Why do we keep making the same mistakes?" Gutfoxx, a popular content creator and streamer, wrote .

Onyx Odds also joined the reaction with a meme depicting Cowboys fans asking Jerry Jones to improve the defense.

In Dallas, Porter joins a defense that has undergone significant changes over the past year. The Cowboys have added defensive linemen Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary, and Kenny Clark through trades, while first-round picks Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence have added young talent to the unit.

Porter now gives Dallas another option in the secondary as the Cowboys look to improve a defense that has struggled through the opening weeks of the season. It remains to be seen whether Porter's addition can change the fortunes of the Cowboys' defense, which now ranks No. 31 in PFN's Defense impact score with a 67.1 grade.

articles.title: What was learned from Dallas' Week 3 loss to the Ravens?
articles.summary: Poor coaching on offense and special teams execution cost the Cowboys a win in Week 3, where their young defense made enough plays to win.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys found a way to lose another game they could've won. They faced off with the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and went toe-to-toe down to the last second of the contest. The Ravens got the ball with seven seconds left after Dallas chose not to go for a touchdown on third-and-goal and also chose not to squib-kick the kickoff. Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers to set up a game-winning field goal for Baltimore.

This was a game dictated by poor decisions on offense and special teams, leaving the door open for the Ravens offense to take the win against a defense decimated by injuries in the defensive backfield. What was learned from the Cowboys' Week 3 contest is that the young defense is improving, but their offense, and especially the coaching staff's decision-making on that side of the ball, has to help win these games. The money is on the offensive side of the ball, so they have to pull wins out of games like this one.

Schottenheimer's play-calling hurt the Cowboys' quick start

Dallas didn't run the ball from the 1-yard line on second or third down . The offense rushed for over seven yards per attempt on the opening drive, with two rushes of eight yards and one of 17 yards. The first dynamic run of the season from anyone not named Dak Prescott . The two plays to get them to the 1-yard line were four-yard runs. Shottenheimer got too cute and called two pass plays, and the Cowboys had to kick a field goal.

On their third drive, up 10-7 on a second-and-six, Shottenheimer split the running back out wide while averaging 6.1 yards per attempt. At a time when the Dallas offense should be protecting its defense, Williams could've been used to run or for a play-action pass. Dallas threw the ball all four plays on that drive and ended up punting. The momentum shifted in favor of Baltimore mainly due to their head coach and play caller.

The offense had chances to put the game away and failed

With the team up 28-24, the defense got a three-and-out, making the Ravens punt the ball back to the Cowboys' offense with 7:29 left in the game. Asking them to milk seven minutes is a lot, but if they can drive down and score a touchdown, they go up two scores with less than five minutes left. Instead, Dallas went three-and-out, running two balls up the middle for a total of four yards and then throwing an incompletion.

After a Baltimore touchdown, Dallas drove down inside the five and couldn't punch it in to win the game. They threw a pass, took a false start penalty, had a QB scramble, and then inexplicably threw it away on third down. The defense was missing multiple defensive backs , so not going for the game-winning touchdown on third down was an awful decision. One long completion and a timeout later, and Dallas loses 34-31.

The Cowboys rookie class is making plays early in their careers

The Dallas defense played well enough to win. Were they still a bad defense overall? Yes, and they should still look to improve the roster on that side of the ball , but given the situation, the defense did enough, and the rookie class is a major part of that. They forced a three-and-out on the first defensive drive, but the Cowboys couldn't score a touchdown from the one-yard line. The defense then caused a turnover on downs when rookie Caleb Downs tackled Derek Henry in the backfield. The rookie class's first big play set up the offense for the early touchdown from the 30-yard line.

In the second half, Jaishawn Barham made two huge stops. One on third-and-one, where he got a tackle for a four-yard loss, and then a goal-to-go tackle of Henry, causing a turnover on downs. LT Overton made a big play at the goal line later, but Baltimore scored two plays after negating the impact of his play. That doesn't change the fact that the defensive rookies are making plays, and the more snaps they get, the better they should get. More experience, better instincts, less reaction to fatigue. The foundational pieces are there.

articles.title: ‘Jerry’s going for it’ – NFL fans react to Dallas Cowboys’ blockbuster Joey Porter Jr. trade
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have made a big win-now move by trading for Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have made a big win-now move by trading for Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The Dallas Cowboys have started the 2026-27 NFL season 1-2, but they have shown signs of promise. The team has what it takes to compete with the best in the league.

That doesn't mean they can't get better, and owner Jerry Jones is seeing to it that they do. The Cowboys have made a huge move late on Wednesday night.

Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been in a contract standoff with the team since the offseason. Dallas has swooped in to take advantage of the situation.

NFL fans think the Dallas Cowboys won the trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers

The Cowboys are reportedly sending the Steelers a 6th-round pick in 2027, and a 2nd-round pick in 2028 for the star cornerback.

After the news came out, fans on social media had a lot to say about it. For the most part, the consensus seems to be that Dallas has gotten a great deal.

"Jerry's going for it, this is just the sort of move we needed," one fan wrote on X. "Jerry I take it all back, this is amazing," another fan claimed.

"Oh my god Jerry's actually going all in," a third fan said. "Dallas has literally zero interceptions all year, so this is a no-brainer," a fourth fan observed.

"Wow! Actually shocked they did it. Now they gotta pay him too," read another comment. "I'm ready for the Cowboys to pay him whatever if he can help this defense out," a sixth fan wrote.

Porter Jr. has been dealing with a back injury to start the 2026 season. Apart from concerns over his health, this looks like it might be an excellent move by Jones and the Cowboys.

articles.body:
After three weeks of action in the NFL, there's been some clarity as to which fantasy football players are good and which are bad. With this information, let's look at which quarterbacks you should consider starting in Week 4 and which quarterback you should hold off on this week.

Start 'Em Quarterbacks in Week 4 of 2026 NFL Season

If you haven't been starting Shough since the end of the 2025 season, you're already missing out. The New Orleans Saints quarterback has been one of the best-performing quarterbacks through the first three weeks of the season, and he's not slowing down anytime soon. Shough went for 255 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders for 24.2 fantasy points.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Shough will be going up against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 4. It's a divisional matchup, but Atlanta's defense has been so-and-so against quarterbacks in fantasy specifically. Shough owners should ride the hot hand and go with the Saints quarterback in Week 4.

Prescott has been one of the better quarterbacks in fantasy this season, averaging around 22 fantasy points through three weeks. Against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 3, he was excellent, throwing for 276 yards and one touchdown for 18.9 fantasy points. One of the more turnover-prone quarterbacks in the league, Prescott has done an excellent job this season limiting his turnovers.

A matchup against the Houston Texans should scare managers on paper, given the team's reputation as one of the best defensive units in the league. However, their passing defense has been surprisingly suspect to start the year. They've given up the eighth-most points to quarterbacks through three weeks. With their passing defense in a bit of a slump as of late, you can count on Prescott to help out your fantasy team.

Brock Purdy's ascension through the NFL ranks has been fascinating to watch. Even with a depleted wide receiver room, the 49ers quarterback is still playing the best football of his career. He's coming off two starts of 28+ fantasy points, the latest of which was a 31.3 FPTS outing in Week 3 where he threw for nearly 300 yards and four touchdowns without a single turnover.

Purdy will take on a tough Denver Broncos defense, yes. But Denver has been middle-of-the-pack in terms of fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks, and a favorable game-state should force the 49ers to throw the ball more.

Sit 'Em Quarterbacks in Week 4 of 2026 NFL Season

Oh, how far Drake Maye has fallen. After an MVP-level campaign in 2025, Maye has severely struggled through the first three weeks of the season. The Patriots quarterback has seven turnovers through three games, most of which were interceptions. Against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3, he threw up a dud, throwing two interceptions, fumbling once, and throwing no touchdowns.

The Buffalo Bills' defense started off slow, but they're starting to show their teeth with a few standout performances. Until Maye can prove that he's shaken off whatever's affecting his play, he's not worth a starting spot in any fantasy league.

The Chargers' Mike McDaniel-Justin Herbert experiment has not worked out well. In fact, it's been absolutely dreadful. The Chargers offense looks like one of the worst units in the league this season, and Herbert's struggles are part of the issue. He's thrown an interception in each of his first three games, and has just averaged 12.6 points to start the year.

A matchup against the in-form Seattle Seahawks defense should make things even worse for Herbert. Like with Maybe, Herbert has to prove that his mojo is back first before being entrusted with a starting role in fantasy leagues again.

Kirk Cousins has shown impeccable form through the first three games of the season. He's been remarkably consistent to start the year, finishing with more than 15 fantasy points in each of the first three weeks of the season. He's coming off an incredible performance against the Saints, throwing for 248 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions.

Unfortunately, Cousins and the Raiders are running into a buzzsaw named the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs defense has allowed the fewest points to quarterbacks in fantasy this season. While Cousins' strong start is a great feel-good story to start the year, there's nothing to indicate that he can overcome one of the stingiest defensive units in the league.
